title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). The tower (114) is G0+ = SL(2,Z) ⊃ Π = Γ(2) (index 6) ⊃ Π0 (index 2) ⊃ Π00 (index 3).

- Π0 is the free group of rank 2 generated by λ0 = [[1,2],[0,1]] and λ1 = [[1,0],[-2,1]] (with λ∞ given by λ0λ1λ∞ = ±1). It is identified with π1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}). Γ(2) = {±1} × Π0, and concretely Π0 = {a ≡ d ≡ 1 mod 4, b, c even}.
- Π00 is the subgroup normally generated in Π0 by λ1λ0^{-1} (and implicitly λ0λ∞^{-1}). It is the kernel of Π0 → Z/3 sending each λi to 1. So Π00 ⊃ [Π0,Π0] and has index 36 in SL(2,Z).

The tower (116) sits inside H = SL(2,Z/12) = SL(2,Z/4) × SL(2,Z/3), of order 1152:
- Π• = sl(2,F2) × SL(2,F3), where sl(2,F2) = ker(SL(2,Z/4) → SL(2,F2)), i.e. the matrices 1+2X with tr X = 0.
- Π0• = sl(2,F2)' × SL(2,F3), where sl(2,F2)' is the Klein group {0, λ0, λ1, λ∞}. It is a complement to the scalar −1 = 1+2I.
- Π00• = sl(2,F2)' × Syl2, where Syl2 is the normal Sylow 2-subgroup of SL(2,F3), of order 8.

This page proves Proposition (114)/(116): the groups in (114) are exactly the inverse images of the groups in (116) under reduction mod 12. The argument has three steps.
1. Reduction maps each group of (114) into the corresponding group of (116). For Π and Π0 this was already known, and reduction mod 4 suffices.
2. Hence the preimage of Π00• contains Π00.
3. Both have index 36: 6·2·3 for Π00, and 1152/32 for the preimage, using surjectivity of SL(2,Z) → SL(2,Z/12). So they are equal. The same index argument works for Π0 (index 12).

Corollary. The map SL(2,Z) → SL(2,Z/12)/Π00•, read as a map to a coset space, factors through G = SL(2,Z)/[Π0,Π0] of the current section. This works because [Π0,Π0] ⊂ Π00 and [Π0,Π0] = [Γ(2),Γ(2)] is normal. The inverse image of Π00• is the subgroup M0 of formulas (99) and (108).

Marginal NB. The group homomorphism SL(2,Z) → SL(2,Z/12) does not itself factor through G+. Otherwise the image of Π0, namely Π0• ⊃ SL(2,F3), would be a quotient of the abelian group Π0/[Π0,Π0] ≅ Z², which is impossible.

Purpose. Π00 is the fundamental group of the cyclic triple cover of P^1 − {0,1,∞} with monodromy (1,1,1), e.g. y³ = x(1−x). Its completion is a genus-1 curve with j = 0, covered by the Fermat cubic. The next page sets this up. The point of the page is to show that this cover is a congruence modular curve of level 12. That prepares a comparison between the metabelian Galois/SL2 action on the extension of Π0^ab by the Tate module of this elliptic curve and the congruence map SL(2,Z)^ → SL(2,Ẑ), within the 'Longue Marche' study of the metabelian quotient of π1(M_{0,3}).
errors: The Sylow 2-subgroup of SL(2,F3) is the quaternion group Q8, not D4. If the previous page's '≃ D4 [?]' is Grothendieck's own, it is a slip; the order 8 and its normality are correct.

sl(2,F2)' is normal in the abelian group sl(2,F2), but it is not normal in SL(2,Z/4). For example, conjugation by [[1,1],[0,1]] sends λ∞ to 1 + λ1, which is scalar plus λ1. Correspondingly Π0 (a ≡ d ≡ 1 mod 4) is not normal in SL(2,Z). So the 'quotient' SL(2,Z/12)/Π00• in the Corollary must be read as a coset space, not a group. The earlier wording 'sous-groupes invariants' has to be understood relative to Γ(2)/Π0, or in a sense not spelled out.

Gap filled by checking: the mod-3 component of λ1λ0^{-1} is [[1,1],[1,2]], which has trace 0, hence order 4, hence lies in Q8. The mod-4 images of λ0 and λ1 lie in the Klein group. So the inclusion of Π00 into the preimage holds. The index-counting argument is correct.

ideas.what: Γ(2) = ±1 × Π0, with Π0 ≅ F2 = π1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) characterised as a level-4 congruence subgroup (preimage of Klein group × SL(2,F3))
ideas.modern_name: free principal congruence-type subgroup (Sanov subgroup), level 4

ideas.what: The index-3 subgroup Π00 ⊂ Π0 (kernel of λi ↦ 1 in Z/3) is the congruence subgroup of level 12 equal to the preimage of Klein × Q8, of index 36 in SL(2,Z)
ideas.modern_name: genus-1 congruence subgroup of level 12, uniformising the j=0 cyclic triple cover of P^1−{0,1,∞} (a quotient of the Fermat cubic)
ideas.usually_credited_to: implicit in the literature on Fermat curves as modular curves (e.g. Rohrlich; the Fermat cubic ≅ X0(27)); the exact level-12 description is in tables of genus-1 congruence subgroups (Cummins–Pauli)

ideas.what: Index-counting proof that a subgroup equals the inverse image of a finite-level subgroup
SL(2,Z) → SL(2,Z/12) does not factor through SL(2,Z)/[Γ(2),Γ(2)], since the image of Π0 is non-abelian

missed.claim: Grothendieck locates a congruence (level 12) subgroup inside the free group π1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) whose cover is the j=0 elliptic curve. He plans, on the next page, to compare the Galois/SL2 action on the resulting second metabelian layer (Tate module of this CM curve) with the congruence map SL(2,Z)^ → SL(2,Ẑ). This is an early instance of studying beyond-metabelian quotients of π1(P^1−3 pts) via CM elliptic curves and congruence quotients. The literature developed related ideas later and independently: Ihara on Fermat Jacobians and the power-series representation, Anderson, Coleman. The specific link drawn here is only an announced program, not carried out.
missed.quote: l'image inverse de Π00' n'est autre que le sous-groupe M0 de (99) (108)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mildly: it frames the Ihara-style Fermat/Jacobi-sum analysis of the metabelian Galois action in terms of congruence subgroups of SL(2,Z). However, the mathematics on this page itself is routine and known.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but routine verification that a specific index-36 subgroup of SL(2,Z) is a level-12 congruence subgroup. Its interest lies in the context (metabelian Longue Marche, link to the j=0 Fermat-type cover and to SL(2,Z)^ → SL(2,Ẑ)), and that thread is only announced on the next page.
transcription_corrections: 'images inverses de Π', Π0'' should be the bullet groups Π•, Π0• of (116). The same applies to Π00' (written Π00• with a dot in the manuscript).
'il suffisait d'examiner Sl(2,Z/4Z), au lieu de Sl(2,Z/12Z)' is confirmed by the image.
In the Corollary the target reads 'Sl(2,Z/12Z)/(Π00• ≃ [Sl(2,F2)]' × Syl2)'; the bracketed factor is the Klein group sl(2,F2)'.
'§ 52 [?]': the section number is partly overwritten in the image ('§ 5?'). It refers to the current § where G = SL(2,Z)/[Π0,Π0] was defined.
Margin: 'Π0• serait un quotient de Π0/[Π0,Π0] et donc serait commutatif' is the likely reading of the 'on serait commutatif' fragment.
